query: Who created the first rocket ship?
answer: No single person gets that title, because it depends on what you count as a "rocket ship." Simple gunpowder rockets go back to medieval China and had no single inventor. For the modern rocket, the key figure is American physicist Robert Goddard. On March 16, 1926, he launched the first liquid-fueled rocket from a farm in Auburn, Massachusetts. It flew for 2.5 seconds and reached 41 feet [1][2]. The first rocket to reach space was a German V-2 on June 20, 1944, which climbed to 175 km. The V-2 was led by Wernher von Braun [3]. If you mean the first rocket that carried a person, that was Vostok 1, which took Yuri Gagarin into orbit on April 12, 1961. Its chief designer was Sergei Korolev [4].
